They support students in developing the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to become responsible, respectful and active citizens in modern Britain.
In line with Department for Education expectations, schools have a duty to actively promote these values as part of preparing young people for life in society. This work is also closely linked to safeguarding and supports students’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development.
At Whitstone School, we ensure that British Values are not only taught but experienced, helping students to understand their importance and apply them in everyday life.

Headteacher Welcome Message
At Whitstone, we believe that every student deserves an exceptional education that prepares them not only for academic success but for a fulfilling life as valued members of our community. Our values—Ambition, Respect, and Excellence—are woven through every aspect of school life, shaping our culture, our curriculum, and the way we support each student to reach their full potential.
We strive to be a school of choice for all families within our community by fostering an inclusive, supportive, and aspirational environment. Our talented, caring and dedicated staff work tirelessly to provide high-quality teaching and tailored support, ensuring that every student thrives both now and in the future.
Together with our community, we are building a sustainable and inspiring future for Whitstone School—one where students are nurtured to be confident, respectful, and ambitious individuals who pursue excellence in all they do.
Thank you for your interest in Whitstone School. I invite you to explore our website to learn more about the opportunities we offer and the values that guide us.
Matthew PikeHeadteacher

The Whitstone Way
Whitstone School Vision and Values: Ambition, Respect, and Excellence
At Whitstone School, our vision is clear and purposeful: We nurture Ambition, we are Respectful, and we strive for Excellence. These core values are the foundation of everything we do, shaping our culture, curriculum, and community engagement.
Nurturing Ambition
Ambition at Whitstone is about inspiring every student to believe in their potential. We provide a supportive environment where students are supported to set challenging personal and academic goals. Our commitment is to ensure every student reaches their full potential, equipped with the skills, knowledge, and confidence to thrive now and in the future. Ambition drives us to innovate teaching and learning and prepare students for the challenges and opportunities of a rapidly changing world.
Being Respectful
Respect is at the heart of our community. We foster a culture where every individual—student, staff, and family—is valued and heard. Respect means embracing diversity, showing empathy, and maintaining a safe, inclusive environment where positive relationships flourish. We expect excellent behaviour both in lessons and across the school, and we work with parents and carers to maintain this respectful environment. Through respect, we build trust, collaboration, and belonging, enabling students and staff to thrive together.
Striving for Excellence
Excellence is our pursuit of the highest standards in all aspects of school life—teaching, learning, behaviour, and leadership. We believe in teaching character and behaviour that allow students to flourish within Whitstone and develop the necessary skills to succeed in future education and the world of work. Our behaviour approach is purposeful and consistent, creating a climate that enables learning and personal growth. Excellence means a relentless pursuit of improvement and the belief that every member of our community contributes to a culture of success.
Our Aspirations
Our Aspirations: Building a School at the Heart of Our Community
Over the next five years, Whitstone School aspires to be the school of choice for all residents within our towns and villages, embedding our values deeply and strengthening our community ties.
Community
We aim to be champions of our community and be championed in return, deepening partnerships with families, local organisations, and public services to enrich students’ education and wellbeing.
Living our Values
Our values of Ambition, Respect, and Excellence will be fully embedded in our work, staffing structures, and curriculum. A strategic rebrand will ensure these values are visible and lived daily.
We will teach and model behaviour that reflects our values, fostering character development and skills essential for students to thrive beyond school. Our curriculum will embed Ambition, Respect, and Excellence, celebrating these values through achievement and community involvement.
Expert Staff and Professional Development
Investing in expert CPD for all staff, we will use evidence-based strategies to intervene effectively and support every student’s progress. Our staff will be empowered to lead and innovate.
This vision aligns with the national emphasis on creating safe, engaging school environments where high expectations and pupil engagement go hand in hand, supported by strong home-school partnerships and evidence-based strategies to improve behaviour and attendance. By embedding these principles, Whitstone School commits to preparing students not only academically but as confident, respectful citizens ready to contribute positively to society.

Wise Up Workshops
Being a parent carer of a child or young person with additional needs can bring extra situations which are challenging to know how to handle. To help support parent carers navigate these a range of workshops have been created by Somerset Parent Carer Forum based on the subjects you have told them would be helpful.
The idea behind the project is to empower parent carers through Workshops for Information, Support and Education. All the workshops will be delivered or co-delivered by someone with lived experience of being a parent carer.
Key topics
Topics to be covered over the year include:
Movement difficulties including dyspraxia
Visual processing and visual stress
Auditory processing and noise sensitivity
Sensory processing
Social development and friendship skills
Understanding and supporting behaviour
Communication support
ADHD and executive functioning
Dyslexia
Autistic masking
Autism and eating difficulties
Autism and toileting
Demand avoidance
Siblings

Their service is free, confidential and impartial.

MFL Mission Statement
The Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) curriculum at Whitstone School is about giving students a positive experience which will equip them with necessary skills that they can develop and use in life beyond the classroom. It encourages students to be more tolerant and curious and have a better understanding of other cultures and their own, while also enabling them to express their ideas and opinions in the target language in both spoken and written forms.
Learning a language at Whitstone school also increases a learner’s confidence and ability to communicate, both in the foreign language and in their own.
There is evidence to show that language learning provides students with improved transferable skills. Learning a language helps to develop listening and problem solving skills and to cope with the unfamiliar, while also improving memory skills. It also helps students to understand the structures and origin of their own language.
We take an inclusive and ambitious approach to learning a language at Whitstone School as we believe it is vitally important that all students gain linguistic and cultural insights, regardless of ability and need. Knowledge is carefully selected and sequenced. Explicit teaching of phonics, reading, listening, speaking and writing, along with vocabulary learning strategies, ensures that pupils are able to make rapid progress.
By the end of a learner’s MFL journey at Whitstone School, whether that be in year 9 or year 11, it is our aim that students will become more tolerant, open-minded global citizens and will demonstrate the resilience and determination to succeed.

Religion, Philosophy and Ethics Mission Statement
At Whitstone School, our Religion, Philosophy and Ethics curriculum inspires curiosity, critical thinking, and empathy. We provide all students with a strong understanding of the world’s main religions, ethical theories, philosophical ideas, and cultural diversity. This equips our young people to reflect thoughtfully on their own beliefs and to engage respectfully with the beliefs of others. Through inquiry, dialogue, and ethical exploration, we foster students’ spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development, support British values, and prepare learners to navigate a diverse and interconnected world with integrity, understanding, and insight.
Success in Religion, Philosophy and Ethics means that every student leaves Whitstone School with a sound grasp of world religions and other worldviews, alongside well-developed skills in empathy, tolerance, and respect for difference and diversity in modern Britain and the wider world. Students studying Religion, Philosophy and Ethics at GCSE level and beyond develop the ability to weigh up different viewpoints, assess the strengths and weaknesses of arguments, and evaluate evidence critically. They also build key transferable skills, such as diplomacy, advocacy, reflection, cultural awareness, and confidence in articulating and defending their views respectfully.
Religion, Philosophy and Ethics, alongside other curriculum areas such as PSHE, contributes significantly to students’ moral, spiritual, and social development. It encourages responsible and caring attitudes and supports students in developing a deeper awareness and understanding of themselves and others.
At Whitstone School, we align our approach with Ofsted’s vision for Religious Education in UK schools, recognising that RE should be “intellectually challenging and personally enriching.” We believe it helps young people develop their beliefs and values and promotes the virtues of respect and empathy, which are essential in our diverse society.

Safeguarding at Whitstone School
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. At Whitstone School we are fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all our students and expect all staff, volunteers and visitors to share this commitment.
We work to ensure that every student feels safe, supported and able to achieve their full potential.
Safeguarding means protecting children from harm, preventing impairment to their health or development and ensuring they grow up in circumstances consistent with the provision of safe and effective care. Our work is guided by the statutory guidance Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) and other Department for Education requirements
Our Safeguarding Commitment
At Whitstone School we:
Safeguarding is embedded across school life and includes areas such as:
Students are supported through lessons, tutor time and assemblies where they learn about:
This helps ensure students understand what behaviour is acceptable and what to do if they are worried about themselves or someone else
Students are encouraged to speak to:
They can do this in person or through the school’s ePraise system.
Students are reminded regularly that no concern is too small to share.
Operation Encompass is a partnership between schools and the police. It ensures that, when the police attend an incident where a child has been exposed to domestic abuse or other significant concerns, the school is informed before the start of the next school day.
This information allows us to provide timely and appropriate support for students who may be experiencing difficulties.
At Whitstone School, a trained member of staff—our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)—acts as the Key Adult for Operation Encompass. They receive this information confidentially and use it to ensure that students are supported in a sensitive and appropriate way.
The Domestic Abuse Act 2021 recognises that children who experience domestic abuse are victims in their own right. We are committed to responding to this and ensuring that every student feels safe, supported and understood.We believe that being part of Operation Encompass strengthens our ability to safeguard students and provide the care and support they need. Safeguarding Training at Whitstone School Safeguarding is a top priority at Whitstone School, and all staff receive regular safeguarding training and updates. Staff are aware of how to identify concerns and how to report them through the school’s safeguarding systems.
Every year, all staff begin the academic year with a safeguarding refresher. These include training in Cyber Security, Female Genital Mutilation Awareness, The Prevent Duty, Domestic Abuse: Children and Young People, Online Safety, Childre Protection in Education and a Keeping Children Safe in Education Part 1 Questionnaire. In addition, staff are required to familiarise themselves with our Whistle Blowing Policy, Keeping Children Safe in Education Part 1, Information Sharing Guidelines and our school’s safeguarding policy.
The Designated Safeguarding Lead and any Deputy Safeguarding Leads have all undertaken Advanced Child Protection training through the Somerset Safeguarding Children Partnership. Designated Safeguarding Team
If you have any safeguarding concerns, please contact the school and ask to speak to a member of the safeguarding team.
If you are worried about a child or young person:
If you have witnessed a crime, you must report this directly to the police and not the school.
Schools must act on all concerns and share information with appropriate agencies when necessary to protect children.
Should you have any concerns in terms of safeguarding relating to the behaviour or welfare of a member of staff, you should immediately contact the Headteacher. Should you feel that your concerns have not been dealt with appropriately by the school or Chair of Trustees, you should contact the Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO), Anthony Goble (0300 123 2224) – email: sdinputters@somerset.gov.uk
We believe safeguarding works best when schools and families work together.
Parents and carers can help by:
We aim to communicate clearly with families and offer guidance where needed.
Key safeguarding policies or those related to safeguarding can be found on our website:
These policies are reviewed regularly to ensure they reflect current legislation and best practice.

Meet the Headteacher
I’m delighted to introduce myself as the Headteacher of Whitstone School. It’s an honour to lead such a wonderful school as Whitstone, and to have the opportunity to work in partnership with students, parents and carers, and the wider community in and around Shepton Mallet.
I’ve recently relocated with my wife and young family to Somerset. We believe Somerset is a fantastic place to call home, and have enjoyed becoming part of the community.
I have worked in education for over 20 years, and the last ten of these have been in positions of senior leadership. Throughout my career I’ve had the opportunity to work at some excellent schools,facilitate some superb educational experiences, and work alongside organisations including the BBC, Ofqual, and the Holocaust Educational Trust. These experiences have strengthened my belief in the power of education to change lives—and in the importance of schools that are ambitious, inclusive, and deeply rooted in their communities.
I hope, in whatever capacity you are viewing this message, that you feel welcome to come to Whitstone School – we will always extend a warm welcome to anyone wishing to see the school in action.

Mrs Payne
Assistant Head Respect
My name is Claire Payne and I am an Assistant Headteacher at Whitstone School, where I lead on Behaviour and Culture and am part of the Safeguarding team.
My passion for teaching began at a very young age. My mum worked at a local secondary school and I grew up seeing the positive impact that working in education could have on young people. That early inspiration led me to study Sports Science and complete my PGCE at Exeter University.
I have now worked in education for 18 years. I began my career as a PE teacher and later moved into pastoral roles, where I also broadened the subjects I taught to include Science and Maths. Throughout my career I have had the privilege of working in schools across Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Dorset, holding roles such as Head of Year, Head of House and PSHE Lead. Before joining Whitstone, I worked as an Associate Assistant Headteacher in my previous school. In September 2024 I moved back to Somerset and joined Whitstone as Assistant Headteacher, which has been a wonderful opportunity.
I feel incredibly fortunate to work in education and am passionate about supporting young people to achieve their potential. I strongly believe in improving life chances, celebrating success and helping students to grow not only academically but also into happy, confident young adults who are ready for the wider world.
Outside of school, I am a wife and a mum to two young children, aged three and five, who certainly keep me busy. As a family we love the outdoors, exploring new places and travelling whenever we can. I also enjoy keeping active through running and going to the gym, and in the past I have played hockey and been involved in rowing teams, alongside a variety of other sports.
Mrs Hunt
Assistant Head Excellence
Outside of school, I am a mum to an energetic 11 year old who has just started secondary school, which definitely keeps me on my toes. I love spending time with him, taking him out and about to different places and making the most of new experiences together. I also enjoy going to the gym, reading, trips to the theatre and cinema, and watching live music whenever I get the chance.
Mrs Boughen-Hunt
Operations and Business Manager
I have worked in the education sector for the past 20 years, previously working in an FE college, an infant school and another secondary school. Alongside my professional role, I have volunteered in school governance for the last 10 years and have been proud to serve as Chair of Governors at a junior school for almost 6 years.
I’m originally from Aberdeenshire and moved to Somerset from Lincoln 27 years ago. Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my family, walking, travelling and visiting up north whenever we can.
We have a fantastic school at the heart of a strong local community. I’m passionate about working together to make a real difference for our students and ensuring they have the best possible opportunities to succeed.
